name: OPT3001 ambient light sensor
description: Texas Instruments ambient light sensor with a human-eye spectral response, measuring 0.01 to 83865.6 lux over I2C with automatic full-scale ranging (16-bit result: 4-bit exponent, 12-bit mantissa). Runs on 1.6–3.6 V only; I2C pins tolerate 5.5 V. Sold as: CJMCU-3001 OPT3001 module (purple, 6-pin header in order VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, INT, ADD), I2C address 0x44 (0x45–0x47 by wiring ADD to VCC, SDA or SCL).
eli5: Measures how bright the light is, in lux, the way your eye sees it. Give it 3.3 V, never 5 V.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 1.6–3.6 V (use 3.3 V; no regulator on the board, 5 V is outside the chip's operating range)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (5.5 V tolerant; resistor network on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, open-drain (5.5 V tolerant; resistor network on the board)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output, open-drain, active low by default; not needed for basic use

pins.name: ADD
pins.description: Address select (chip ADDR pin): GND = 0x44 (board default), VCC = 0x45, SDA = 0x46, SCL = 0x47

supplierQuery: CJMCU-3001 OPT3001 ambient light sensor module I2C
buildNotes: Header order on the CJMCU-3001 is VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, INT, ADD: SCL comes before SDA.
Power it from 3.3 V only: the OPT3001 operates at 1.6–3.6 V (absolute maximum 6 V). Its SDA, SCL and ADDR inputs tolerate up to 5.5 V.
The chip powers up shut down (configuration 0xC810, M = 00): write the configuration register before reading, e.g. 0xCE10 for auto range, 800 ms, continuous.
Result register 0x00: lux = 0.01 × 2^E × R, where E = bits 15–12 and R = bits 11–0. In auto range (RN = 1100b) the chip picks E itself; with RN 0–11 E equals RN.
A conversion takes up to 880 ms (800 ms mode) or 110 ms (100 ms mode); the result reads 0 until the first one ends.
Reading the configuration register clears the conversion-ready flag (CRF).
Check the IDs: register 0x7E reads 0x5449 ('TI') and 0x7F reads 0x3001.
The simulator models the chip with a fixed full-scale range of 10483.2 lux (RN = 1000b, 2.56 lux per count), which the example selects; in auto range the real chip reports finer steps at low light.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from opt3001 import OPT3001

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
# 0x44 with ADD at GND; fixed 10483.2 lx full-scale range (RN = 8, 2.56 lx per count), 800 ms, continuous
sensor = OPT3001(i2c, range_number=8)
while True:
    print('Lux=%.2f' % sensor.lux())
    time.sleep(1)
